To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

IDEC-C2b8, an anti-CD20 chimeric mouse/human monoclonal antibody, is cytotoxic to lymphoma cells via direct lysis and complement-dependent cellular cytotoxity, and also via antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxcity.

the cytotoxic effect of IDEC-C2b8 in CD20-positive lymphoma cell lines is caused by direct cytotoxicity (DC), complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC), and antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxcity (ADCC).
IDEC-C2 B8 induced a combined direct cytotoxic and complement-dependent cellular cytotox-icity, and that antibody-dependent cellular cytoto- xicity was observed in all cell lines tested.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of cytolytic effects of chimeric IDEC-C2b8 monoclonal antibody against CD20 antigen.
the mechanisms of action of chimaeric mouse human anti- CD20 monoclonal antibodies in CD20-expressed lymphoma cell lines in vitro.
the mechanism of action and the potential therapeutic efficacy of IDEC-C2 B8 in the treatment of B cell lymphomas and chronic lymphocytic leukemia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cytotoxicity of IDEC-C2b8 against CD20-expressin lymphoma cell lines is mediated by three different mechanisms: direct cytotoxicity (in the presence of complement), CDCC, and antibody-dependent cellular cytolyticity (in the absence of complement), and that these mechanisms are responsible for the in vivo antitumoral effects of the antibody.

the cytotoxicity of IDEC-C2b8 in lymphoma cell lines is due to a combination of direct cytotoxicity (in CD20-expressin lymphoma cells) and antibody-dependent cell cytotoxicity (against CD20-expressig lymphoma cells).
the chimeric mouse/human monoclonal antibody, IDEC-C2b8 (Rituximab) is an effective and specific agent for treatment of CD20-ex-pressing non-Hodgkin's lymphoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cytotoxicity of IDEC-C2b8 is a combination of direct and antibody-dependent cytotoxicity.
CD20 is an ideal target for the treatment of B cell malignancies, because of its high density and homogeneous expression.
IDEC-C2b8 is a potent antibody that can induce both direct and ADCC and CDCC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mechanism of cytolytic action of the anti-CD20 antibody is complex and involves direct lysis, complement-dependent cytotoxicity, and antibody-dependent cellular cytolytic action.
CD20 is not only a marker but also an important functional molecule in the B-cell receptor complex, and that it plays a role in cell survival.
CD20 expression alone is not a sufficient condition for the efficacy of IDEC-C2b8.
